items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...music of Jean Goldkette or — [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah or Bix or —

ctx.x: All in the same concert from nineteen twenty whatever it was on the banjo to this stuff, yeah. So there aren’t many guys that can do that so that was good, good for me.

We were having a discussion with a few people today about traditional jazz and they feel it’s not well represented in the jazz education scene. And I’m trying to figure out why. Why is the music of Charlie Parker and John Coltrane given more artistic weight than, you know the music of Jean Goldkette or —
